title: Holding TAB too long when alt-tabbing between editor windows breaks hover tooltips
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.8.dev1.official [ebbf577a0], v4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb], v4.7.dev3.official [60fff00a6]
- Not reproducible in: v4.7.dev2.official [778cf54da]

### System information

Godot v4.7.1.stable - Linux Mint 22.3 (Zena) on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (RPL-P) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700H (20 threads) - 15.24 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When alt-tabbing between editor windows, holding `TAB` longer than `ALT` will cause tooltips to not appear in whichever window receives focus. Even a fraction of a second longer is enough, which made this particularly tricky to track down as the cause. This seems to only affect tooltips that pull information from documentation (e.g. properties in the inspector, signals in the signals dock, certain highlighted text in scripts in the script editor, etc). Tooltips such as those for nodes in the scene dock, files in the filesystem dock, and menus are not affected.

Importantly(?), this does NOT happen when switching to an editor window from any other application, only when switching between editor windows.

Seems related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/118341 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/118826, particularly the former, but not identical (I'm only using a single workspace; I'm on X11, not Wayland; it's unclear if those issues apply to tooltips beyond just inspector properties and scripts). Those were both marked fixed by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118895, so I think something else is going on here.

EDIT (hit "submit" too soon): **This only occurs on X11.** Wayland does not show this behavior. Tested with Cinnamon 6.6.7 which uses X11 by default but offers a "Wayland (Experimental)" option.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the editor (no project required)
2. Verify that documentation tooltips appear when hovering appropriate items
3. Pop out any dock/editor that can generate such tooltips into a separate window
4. Verify that these tooltips appear in this new window
5. Use `ALT + TAB` to switch focus to the other editor window, making sure to release **`ALT` before `TAB`**.
6. Verify that documentation tooltips no longer appear in this new window
7. Repeat 5-6 to see the behavior occur in both windows
8. Use `ALT + TAB` to switch focus to the other editor window, making sure to release **`TAB` before `ALT`**
9. Verify that documentation tooltips now appear in whatever window you just switched to

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A
